descripcion_geo: Kingdom in southern Arabia (present-day Yemen or northern Ethiopia), famous for its trade in spices, incense and gold.
importancia_estrategica: Center of the incense trade; The Queen of Sheba visited Solomon and is a symbol of wisdom that seeks the truth.

historias.titulo: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon
historias.descripcion: The Queen of Sheba travels to Jerusalem with camels loaded with spices, gold and precious stones to test Solomon with riddles.
The queen of Sheba gives Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold, many spices, and precious stones; Solomon gave her everything she asked for.

historias.titulo: Sheba in the prophets and psalms
historias.descripcion: Psalm 72 and the prophets Isaiah and Jeremiah mention Sheba as a distant land that will bring tribute to the messianic king.

personajes.descripcion: He sought the wisdom of Solomon; Jesus cites her as an example of one who seeks the truth (Mt 12:42).
He impressed the queen of Sheba with his wisdom, his palace, and the Temple.
Hiram's ships brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks from Ophir (possibly Sheba).

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Sheba: relevant geographic region in the Old Testament.

judaismo.descripcion: The queen of Sheba came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon (1 Kgs 10:1).
judaismo.significado_teologico: The queen of Sheba came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon (1 Kgs 10:1).

cristianismo.descripcion: Jesus says that the queen of the south will rise in judgment and condemn those who reject him who is greater than Solomon (Mt 12:42).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Jesus says that the queen of the south will rise in judgment and condemn those who reject him who is greater than Solomon (Mt 12:42).

islam.descripcion: Bilqis (the queen of Sheba) is a legendary figure in Islamic tradition; the Qur'an narrates his story in relation to Solomon (Sulaiman) (Cor 27:22-44).
islam.significado_teologico: Bilqis (the queen of Sheba) is a legendary figure in Islamic tradition; the Qur'an narrates his story in relation to Solomon (Sulaiman) (Cor 27:22-44).
